output.brief: Last week's 5xx rate (0.41%) is inside the normal band. The preceding 26 weeks averaged 0.354% with an upper edge of 0.482%, and several ordinary weeks were higher. The error budget burn was 0.82x, well below the 2x paging threshold. The dashboard matches raw logs, so the rise is not a counting artefact. Customer bookings did not change and support logged no complaints. Dario's finding that new pods error more than old ones is a rollout warm-up effect. Pods with empty caches send reads to the replica and time out. The same gap appeared in all five recent rollouts, including a config-only redeploy, so it does not point to v4.18. Pods of the same age on different versions were never compared. That means a v4.18 fault is not proven, but nothing shows one. I recommend no rollback, no alert muting, and no replica move. Record the week as normal and run the standard check on the following week. Muting the burn-rate page would remove the safeguard that would catch a real problem. Confidence is fairly high, but the replica and partner-sync causes were not tested, so they stay open. If next week exceeds the band, investigate then.
